title: Plan a trip on W10 (godown) and M7 (manager): one additive planning read (crew + packed bills not on an open trip), trips.create / stops.add from both apps with retry-stable ids, the double-plan guard made role-proof through one shared ids-only helper, and W7 builds each load sheet for a trip (tripId) from that trip's shops
rootCause:
ONE cause for both ids: no screen plans a trip, so nothing gives the godown a trip to build a load sheet for. I re-read every citation below on main (117717c = b59bbf0 + docs). Each holds within ±3 lines unless marked.

DOS-131 (no UI path):
- No frontend call exists: `git grep "trips.create|stops.add" frontend/*-app` finds nothing.
- W10 `frontend/warehouse-app/app/load/trips.tsx` offers only startLoading/depart (:45-70, :110-131). Its header (:4-8) says the godown 'may NOT create the round'. That contradicts:
  - docs/22 §8 row 2026-09-12 (DOS-043, line 269): 'The warehouse role keeps creating trips, adding stops and starting loading'.
  - docs/23:406: 'W10 Trips: create, start loading'.
- M7 `frontend/manager-app/app/fulfilment/load-out.tsx` offers approve, cancel and EWB only. The manager '/fulfilment' tab row has three tabs (src/nav.ts:65-68). O18 is a register.
- The backend already supports it:
  - `trips.service.ts:178-266 create` and `:508-548 addStop`.
  - `permissions.ts:658,669` give both to TRIP_PLANNERS (:189-194).
  - DeliveryModule and the `delivery` contract key are mounted on warehouse-service (definitions.ts:221-260) and manager-service (:137-160).
  - The existing spec 'plans a trip from the godown with stops, planned deliveries and a TRIP number' (delivery.spec.ts:555) already has a warehouse token create a trip. Live pg_policies trips_insert and trip_stops_write_insert admit warehouse.

The design's 'no contract change' is incomplete. Code and the live policies prove three gaps:
(1) The godown cannot name a driver.
  - CreateTripInput.driverId is required (contracts/delivery.ts:683-693), and TripSchema carries a bare driverId (:379-380).
  - `tenancy.staff.list` is BACK_OFFICE (permissions.ts:373). `reporting.registers.deliveryPerformance` is CREW_PERFORMANCE_READERS (:893).
  - RLS is not the obstacle: memberships_read is tenant-only, and users_visible admits any user with a membership in the tenant. The obstacle is the matrix.
  - Widening staff.list would hand the godown every phone and username (listStaff selects both, tenancy.service.ts:104-140).
(2) No read answers 'packed bills not yet on a trip'.
  - `warehouse.packs.list` returns every pack, dispatched ones included, ordered desc(id) (DOS-133). OrderSchema has no invoice.
  - A planned bill is a `deliveries` row with outcome null. Live `deliveries_read` admits owner, manager, accountant, system, the trip's crew or the shop, never warehouse. The spec pins `stops[].deliveries = []` for the packer (delivery.spec.ts:583-584).
  - Orders, warehouse and billing are upstream of delivery and may not read those tables, so only the delivery module can answer.
(3) A latent double-plan hole that the new W10 path opens.
  - insertStop's 'already planned on another open trip' select (trips.service.ts:973-988) runs under the caller's RLS. For warehouse, `deliveries_read` returns no rows, so the 409 never fires.
  - The only unique index on invoice is (tenant_id, stop_id, invoice_id) (pg_indexes deliveries_stop_invoice_idx).
  - The planned-row insert right after the select already runs as system (:1000-1016 asSystemRole); the select does not.
  - The same hole exists for a `delivery` caller, who sees only its own trips' rows. It also exists inside ONE create whose two stops carry the same bill.

DOS-137 (sheet never linked):
- `frontend/warehouse-app/app/load/index.tsx:60-68` create() sends no tripId. W7 picks an inventory vehicle location (:50-54 `inventory.locations.list kind=vehicle`, :161-177), not a trip.
- `load-sheets.service.ts:202` stores `tripId: input.tripId ?? null`. Nothing attaches a trip later: the schema comment 'delivery attaches the trip afterwards' was never built.
- Every reader keys on trip_id:
  - `confirmedForTrip` (:613-632) feeds `delivery.mappers.ts:574,590-591` (loadConfirmedAt, loadSheetIds).
  - The crew's D1 reads local `load_sheets where trip_id = ?` (delivery-app/app/index.tsx:87-97, panel :316-343), pulled by `registerPull('load_sheets')` (warehouse.module.ts:69).
- dos_qa: 5 of 180 load_sheets have trip_id NULL (tarsun 2, a probe tenant 3).

Second contributing cause checked and ruled out:
- insertStop is called only from create and addStop (git grep).
- No worker job, outbox consumer or sync handler creates trips or links a sheet to a trip.
- The crew's pull of load_sheets is not trip-filtered (fieldOnly = last 30 days), so a linked sheet reaches D1 with no further change.

JSDoc:

contractChange:
ADDITIVE, one new procedure: `delivery.trips.planning`, GET /delivery/trip-planning. New schemas TripPlanningInput, TripPlanningOutput, PlanningCrewSchema and PlanningBillSchema in contracts/delivery.ts.

Unchanged: every existing schema, route and output. trips.create, stops.add and loadSheets.create keep their shapes; W7 uses the already-optional `tripId`.

Why it cannot be avoided (the architect design said no contract change):
(1) The warehouse role has no read that names the crew:
  - `tenancy.staff.list` is BACK_OFFICE (permissions.ts:373) and returns phones and usernames.
  - deliveryPerformance.driverName is CREW_PERFORMANCE_READERS (:893).
  - CreateTripInput.driverId is required.
  So W10 'create' (docs/22 §8 2026-09-12, docs/23 W10) is impossible without a new read.
(2) Only the delivery module can answer 'packed bills not yet on a trip', because it owns `deliveries` and `trips`. Orders, warehouse and billing are upstream. `deliveries_read` RLS hides planned rows from warehouse, so no client-side combination of existing reads can exclude them.

One read serves both apps identically and costs one bounded page per call. The route is `/delivery/trip-planning`, not `/delivery/trips/planning`, which GET `/delivery/trips/{id}` would shadow.
